name: Machinery Maintenance & Repair

objectives.text: Identify the fluids, filters, and lubrication points on a piece of farm machinery
Explain how preventive maintenance extends machine life, reduces breakdowns, and improves operator safety
Select and safely use the correct hand tools and shop equipment for basic machinery maintenance tasks
Demonstrate a routine preventive maintenance service, including fluid level checks and fluid and filter changes
Lubricate machinery grease fittings using the correct grease and the interval specified by the manufacturer
Interpret an equipment operator's manual and maintenance schedule to determine required service tasks and intervals
Identify common fastener types, thread sizes, and bolt grades used on farm machinery
Perform a pre-operation walk-around inspection of a machine using a written checklist
Explain lockout/tagout procedures and the stored energy hazards that must be controlled before servicing machinery
Describe proper handling, storage, recycling, and disposal of used oil, filters, coolant, and other shop wastes
Record completed maintenance and repairs in a service log as part of a supervised agricultural experience
Select oils, greases, and coolants by viscosity grade and service classification for specific machine applications
Compare the operating principles and wear characteristics of belts, chains, gears, bearings, seals, and drive shafts
Assess belts, chains, sprockets, hoses, bearings, and nozzles for wear and damage against manufacturer service specifications
Perform scheduled preventive maintenance on equipment and power units following the manufacturer's service manual
Diagnose the cause of a machinery malfunction using a systematic troubleshooting sequence and manufacturer guidelines
Use precision measuring tools and a torque wrench to measure component wear and tighten fasteners to specification
Replace a worn belt, bearing, or chain drive component and set correct alignment and tension
Prepare a machine for seasonal storage and return it to service following manufacturer procedures
Design a written lockout/tagout and service procedure plan for maintaining a specific machine in the school shop or SAE operation
Evaluate malfunctioning machinery electrical components such as batteries, lighting, fuses, and wiring using a multimeter and service manual
Calculate the annual and per-hour maintenance and repair costs of a piece of farm equipment
Justify a repair-versus-replace decision for a piece of equipment using cost, downtime, and reliability data
Create a fleet maintenance schedule and record system for a farm, agribusiness, or SAE operation

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording several and moving troubleshooting to grade 10 and splitting the grade 12 item into a cost-based repair-versus-replace decision and a fleet record system design. Added middle-grade foundations: tool selection, grease lubrication, fasteners, pre-operation inspection, lockout/tagout awareness, waste disposal, and SAE service logs. Added high school competencies tied to AFNR standards: lubricant selection, comparing drive components, assessing wear to spec, scheduled service by manual, precision measurement and torque, seasonal storage, a LOTO and service plan, electrical component testing, and maintenance cost calculation. Left engine overhaul, tractor systems, and hydraulics to the sibling sub-topics.
